subject: DPA appendix: ownership matrix for customer keys + dataflow clarifications
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@medsync.health>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, procurement@medsync.health
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: DPA appendix: key custody + dataflow questions

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal/security team reviewed the standard DPA and asked for a short appendix specific to private deployments (VPC / on-prem) that clarifies:

- Ownership and custody of cryptographic keys (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed)
- What operators can access in a break-glass emergency and how that access is logged
- Whether any model weights or derived artifacts could be transferred or processed outside our VPC
- A simple dataflow/ownership matrix mapping customer data categories to where they reside and what Redwood can/does access

Attached is a short checklist from our side. Can Redwood provide a draft appendix that we can iterate on, and confirm whether you're willing to accept customer-managed keys (we'd prefer a true BYOK flow with no Redwood plaintext access) or whether the only option is escrow/key-escrow under a limited set of circumstances?

We'd like to get this wrapped prior to the SOW sign-off next week.

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Gomez
Sr. Counsel, MedSync Health
maria.gomez@medsync.health
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: medsync_dpa_checklist.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@medsync.health>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA appendix: key custody + dataflow questions

Hi Maria —

Really appreciate the clear checklist — that's super helpful. We've attached an initial draft appendix that reflects Redwood's current private-deploy options. High-level answers up front:

- BYOK (customer-managed KMS) is supported. In that mode Redwood never holds the customer key material in plaintext. We integrate with customer KMS via a customer-provided key encryption endpoint and only retain encrypted key references.
- We offer an optional KMS-escrow workflow (used rarely) under a narrowly scoped break-glass addendum; escrow access requires multi-party approval and is fully logged to an immutable audit trail.
- Operator access: for on-prem/VPC deployments, Redwood operators do not have network access to customer-controlled subnets by default. Break-glass remote-support requires a customer-initiated tunnel and explicit short-lived credentials; all sessions are recorded and stored for 7 years.
- Model/data flows: no model weights or derived embeddings are exported from your VPC unless explicitly enabled in writing. Our draft includes a dataflow ownership matrix as CSV (attached) — please review.

Next steps: I've proposed language around the customer key lifecycle and an example escrow clause in the attached Word doc. Can you confirm whether MedSync needs HSM-backed keys (we support both cloud HSM and on-prem HSM integrations) and whether your legal team wants tighter restrictions on operator logs retention longer than 7 years?

If helpful, Marcus Lin (copied privately) can join a 30-minute call to walk through the matrix tomorrow.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood_dpa_appendix_draft_v1.docx (Word, 28KB); dataflow_ownership_matrix.csv (CSV, 4KB)

Hi Maria / Jasmine —

Thanks for the note. A few clarifications from the product / security side to bake into the appendix:

1) BYOK integration: we support both KMIP-backed on-prem HSM and cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). In BYOK mode the keys never leave the customer HSM in plaintext. Redwood stores only a 1:1 encrypted key reference and a key metadata blob (algorithm, key id, usage policy).

2) Break-glass: the appendix should enumerate the exact audit fields we log (timestamp, operator id, session transcript, nominated customer approval token). We also capture a cryptographic hash of any temporary keys used for the session so customers can validate integrity.

3) Dataflow: we recommend a short "no-export-by-default" clause plus an explicit list of allowed exports (diagnostics bucket, telemetry sanitized for PII, model telemetry only with explicit opt-in). We'll provide a short CSV mapping: PII / Health Identifiers -> resides in Customer VPC -> Redwood has access: No (unless explicit opt-in).

4) Subprocessors: the appendix must reference the base DPA subprocessors section and call out that for private deployments there are no new subprocessors unless agreed in writing (e.g., hardware maintenance partner with access windows).

Marcus, can you add a one-line implementation note on how rollback access is handled for model cache in private deployments?

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Thanks Jasmine / Laura — this is helpful. A few quick confirmations before we route to our CISO for sign-off: 

- MedSync requires HSM-backed customer keys (on-cloud HSM in our AWS account is acceptable).
- 7 years of audit log retention is fine. We will ask for a quarterly attestation that break-glass was not used (or that details are provided if used).
- Please add an explicit line to the appendix: "Redwood will not perform model weight exports or extract embeddings outside the customer VPC unless MedSync issues an explicit written instruction."

Procurement: please review the DocuSign link below and queue the SOW for signature once legal confirms the appendix text.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/r/ABC123-redwood-med-sync

Appreciate the quick turnaround. If you can update the Word draft with the HSM acceptance language and the no-export sentence, we'll push to our CISO on Monday.

Best,
Maria
